boundaries: Context supplies the purpose-specific relevance boundary; Context Profile supplies reusable construction and resolution policy.
A Profile can govern many Contexts while retaining its own owner, version, lifecycle, and challenge route.
Profile revisions do not silently reinterpret existing Context versions.
claim_ceiling: This candidate defines Context Profile for Step 3 review only and has no admission or downstream activation effect.
residue_refs: Artifact Type rebinding and admission remain separate.

scope.applicability: A Context Profile is a reusable versioned policy contract that constrains how purpose-bound Contexts may be constructed and resolved through permitted anchor kinds, cardinalities, identity fields, source rules, freshness, exclusions, succession, and challenge handling.
exclusions: It is not a Context instance and carries no Product, Project, Goal, purpose-bound Context identity, resolved source selection, or consumer-specific view.
Profile conformance does not create a Context or prove that resolution inputs are current.
This Definition does not admit a carrier, instance, relation, runtime, consumer, publication, or deployment.

examples: profile:product-project-context/v1 permits exactly one Product anchor, an optional Project anchor, explicit source digests, a 24-hour freshness ceiling, and successor-only revision.
domain_context.explanation: Context Profile receives its own positive meaning so its carrier no longer borrows a broader Definition as its primary semantic identity.

testable_conditions: Every Context Profile declares allowed anchor kinds, cardinalities, identity rules, source constraints, freshness, succession, owner, and challenge route.
A Context claiming conformance names one exact Profile version.
